cohort: 102,589 women who had a cesarean delivery after 24 weeks' gestational age at 2 hospitals in Sydney, Australia
finding: The increase in cesarean delivery rates from 19% to 30% over a 30-year period was largely attributable to changes in maternal demographic and clinical factors, particularly nulliparity, age, body mass index, and the management of high-risk pregnancies.
mod_finding: The study found a significant increase in cesarean delivery rates over a 30-year period, largely attributable to changes in maternal demographics (age, BMI, parity) and the management of high-risk pregnancies.
